items.title: Israeli airstrike kills displaced family in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Report: At least six dead in Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon

items.description:
Israeli airstrikes killed a displaced family in the southern Lebanese town of Kfar Hatta on Sunday, as the military intensified its aerial campaign across the country and warned it would strike near the main Syria-Lebanon border crossing.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported six members of one family were killed in the strike on Kfar Hatta, a town from which the Israeli military had earlier ordered evacuations. The family had been displaced from Kfar Tibnit in the Nabatieh district and was sheltering in the town when the attack occurred. A Lebanese civil defense source told AFP the family had been waiting for a relative to pick them up so they could leave. At least three more people were killed in a separate airstrike elsewhere in southern Lebanon on Sunday morning.[1][2][3]

items.title: Indonesia receives slain UN peacekeepers as UNIFIL threats mount

featured_image.name: Prabowo Condemns Killing of Indonesian UN Peacekeepers in ...

items.description:
Indonesia on Saturday received the remains of three United Nations peacekeepers killed during Israel's military operations in southern Lebanon, as mounting attacks on UN personnel drew international condemnation.

The coffins of the fallen soldiers, draped in the Indonesian flag, arrived at Jakarta's international airport and were carried into a ceremonial hall by uniformed comrades in a solemn ceremony attended by President Prabowo Subianto.[1][2][3]

items.title: Durov vows Telegram will evade Russia's ban, cites Iran parallels

featured_image.name: Meet Pavel Durov, the Billionaire Founder of Telegram ...

items.description:
Telegram co-founder Pavel Durov said on Saturday that approximately 50 million Iranians continue to use the messaging app through VPNs despite a years-long government ban, calling them "50 million members of the Digital Resistance in Iran." The remarks came as part of a broader post in which Durov also addressed Russia's recent decision to block Telegram, drawing a direct parallel between the two countries' failed censorship strategies.[1][2]

"Iran banned Telegram years ago, with a result similar to Russia," Durov wrote on his Telegram channel. "The government hoped for mass adoption of its surveillance messaging apps, but instead VPN usage exploded." He added that "the whole nation is mobilized to circumvent these absurd restrictions" and pledged that Telegram would adapt its traffic to become harder to detect and block.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's internet blackout is now longest on record at 37 days

featured_image.name: Why Iran keeps turning off the internet during mass protests

items.description:
Iran's nationwide internet shutdown has become the longest government-imposed blackout ever recorded in any country, entering its 37th consecutive day on Saturday after 864 hours of near-total disconnection, according to global internet monitor NetBlocks.

"Iran's internet blackout is now the longest nation-scale internet shutdown on record in any country, exceeding all other comparable incidents in severity," NetBlocks said in a post on X on April 5. The organization noted that while some countries have experienced intermittent or regional shutdowns over longer periods, no nation had previously imposed a continuous nationwide blackout of this duration.[1][2]

items.title: Pope Leo celebrates first Easter with call to 'lay down' weapons

featured_image.name: Pope Leo's Easter Sunday 2026 Holy Mass, Urbi et Orbi ...

items.description:
Pope Leo XIV marked his first Easter as leader of the Catholic Church on Sunday, celebrating Mass before some 50,000 people in a sun-drenched St. Peter's Square before delivering a pointed appeal for world leaders to choose peace over conflict.[1][2]

"Let those who have weapons lay them down!" the pope declared from the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica in his Urbi et Orbi message — the traditional Easter address "to the city and the world." "Let those who have the power to unleash wars choose peace — not a peace imposed by force, but through dialogue, not with the desire to dominate others, but to encounter them!"[1]

items.title: Israel halted strikes, shared intel to aid US airman rescue in Iran

featured_image.name: A US F-15 is down in Iran, search and rescue underway

items.description: Israel provided critical intelligence support and suspended its own airstrikes to help the United States rescue a downed F-15E crew member stranded deep inside Iran, an Israeli military official confirmed on Sunday. The disclosure sheds new light on the close coordination between the two allies during one of the most dramatic military operations of the five-week-old war.

items.description: The United States Air Force has lost at least seven manned aircraft since the start of its war with Iran, CNN reported on Saturday, a tally that undercuts the Trump administration's repeated assertions of near-total air dominance over the country.[1][2]

items.title: Trump's 48-hour Iran ultimatum expires Monday as strikes hit Mahshahr

featured_image.name: Trump gives Iran 48-hour deadline to reopen Strait of Hormuz or face new ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his confrontation with Iran on Saturday, warning Tehran it has 48 hours to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating military consequences, as U.S. and Israeli forces struck Iran's largest petrochemical complex and ceasefire talks collapsed.

"Remember when I gave Iran ten days to MAKE A DEAL or OPEN UP THE HORMUZ STRAIT," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Saturday morning. "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!" The ultimatum sets a Monday, April 6, deadline that Trump has repeatedly extended since first threatening to destroy Iran's power plants on March 21.[1][2][3]

items.title: Navy SEALs rescue downed F-15E airman from Iran

featured_image.name: Trump confirms both military officers missing in Iran have been saved

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced early Sunday that U.S. Special Operations forces had successfully rescued the second crew member from an F-15E Strike Eagle shot down over Iran, capping a two-day operation that military officials called one of the most challenging in U.S. special operations history.

"WE GOT HIM!" Trump wrote on Truth Social, describing the rescued airman as a "brave Warrior" who had been "behind enemy lines in the treacherous mountains of Iran, being hunted down by our enemies, who were getting closer and closer by the hour."[1][2]
